title: Rhetoric
extract: Rhetoric is the art of persuasion. It is one of the three ancient arts of discourse, along with grammar and logic. As a discipline, rhetoric studies the techniques that speakers and writers use to inform, persuade, and motivate audiences. Its central aim is to identify the available means of persuasion in any given case.
locke: My friends, let us not mistake noise for knowledge.
Consider, soberly, what is actually known: Rhetoric is the art of persuasion. This is not cause for panic; it is cause for thought.

We are urged to be afraid. Yet the record says only this: As a discipline, rhetoric studies the techniques that speakers and writers use to inform, persuade, and motivate audiences. A measured nation does not riot at a sentence.

↳ My opponent would set the house alight to be rid of a draught. Its central aim is to identify the available means of persuasion in any given case. — read it again, slowly. There is no monster here, only a problem we can govern.
So let us govern ourselves first: weigh, do not shout; reason, do not rage. The long peace is built of patience.
demosthenes: They will call this calm. I call it the quiet before they take what is yours.
Look at what they bury in their careful words: rhetoric is the art of persuasion. Does that sound like nothing to you? It is everything.

Here is what they would never shout from the rooftops: as a discipline, rhetoric studies the techniques that speakers and writers use to inform, persuade, and motivate audiences. And still they tell you to sit down and be quiet.

↳ My gentle opponent counsels patience. Patience! Its central aim is to identify the available means of persuasion in any given case. — by the time his "long peace" arrives, the moment to act will be a memory. Caution is how the slow are conquered.
So rise. Speak. Demand. The calm voices have had their century — the hour belongs to those awake enough to seize it.
